title.en: Inside HTTPS: TLS 1.3 Handshake and Trust Chains
title.ms: Di Dalam HTTPS: TLS 1.3 Handshake dan Rantaian Kepercayaan

summary.en: Ever wonder why that little padlock, or the icon some browsers now show instead, doesn’t guarantee a trustworthy site? HTTPS does three things: it hides your data, it detects tampering, and it proves you’re talking to the right server. The padlock only tells you the TLS handshake succeeded and the certificate matches the hostname.
summary.ms: Pernah terfikir kenapa padlock kecil itu, atau ikon yang kini dipaparkan oleh sesetengah pelayar, tidak menjamin laman yang boleh dipercayai? HTTPS melakukan tiga perkara: ia menyembunyikan data anda, mengesan gangguan, dan membuktikan anda sedang bercakap dengan pelayan yang betul. Padlock hanya memberitahu anda bahawa TLS handshake berjaya dan sijil sepadan dengan nama hos.

chapters.en: Certificates and the Chain of Trust

chapters.ms: TLS 1.3 handshake dalam satu round trip
Daripada handshake kepada HTTP yang disulitkan

code.title: inspect_tls.py
code.code:
"""See what a real TLS handshake negotiated, and the certificate chain of trust.

    python inspect_tls.py example.com
    python inspect_tls.py github.com 443

Standard library only (Python 3.13+). If verification fails on Windows with
"unable to get local issuer certificate", run `pip install certifi` and retry:
Windows downloads some root certificates on demand, so Python may not see them yet.
"""
import socket
import ssl
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def trust_store() -> tuple[ssl.SSLContext, str]:
    try:
        import certifi
        return ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()), "certifi (Mozilla) bundle"
    except ImportError:
        return ssl.create_default_context(), "operating system store"


def decode(der: bytes) -> dict:
    # The stdlib can only parse certificates from a file, so write the DER bytes out as PEM.
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".pem", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(ssl.DER_cert_to_PEM_cert(der))
    return ssl._ssl._test_decode_cert(f.name)


def field(cert: dict, part: str) -> str:
    d = dict(x[0] for x in cert.get(part, ()))
    return d.get("commonName") or d.get("organizationName", "?")


def main(host: str, port: int = 443) -> None:
    ctx, store = trust_store()
    with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=10) as raw:
        # wrap_socket runs the whole handshake: ClientHello (with SNI = host and key shares),
        # ServerHello, then the encrypted certificate, CertificateVerify and Finished.
        with ctx.wrap_socket(raw, server_hostname=host) as tls:
            cipher, _, bits = tls.cipher()
            print(f"Connected to {host}:{port}")
            print(f"  protocol    : {tls.version()}")
            print(f"  cipher      : {cipher} ({bits}-bit AEAD key)")
            print(f"  trust store : {store}")

            chain = tls.get_verified_chain()
            print(f"\nChain of trust ({len(chain)} certificates, server first):")
            for i, der in enumerate(chain):
                c = decode(der)
                role = "server" if i == 0 else ("root (trusted)" if i == len(chain) - 1 else "intermediate")
                print(f"  [{i}] {role:<15} {field(c, 'subject')}")
                print(f"      signed by       {field(c, 'issuer')}")
                print(f"      valid until     {c['notAfter']}")

            leaf = tls.getpeercert()
            expires = datetime.fromtimestamp(ssl.cert_time_to_seconds(leaf["notAfter"]), timezone.utc)
            names = [v for k, v in leaf.get("subjectAltName", ()) if k == "DNS"]
            print(f"\nServer certificate covers: {', '.join(names[:5])}{' ...' if len(names) > 5 else ''}")
            print(f"It expires in {(expires - datetime.now(timezone.utc)).days} days.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    main(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 443)

title.en: What Really Happens When You Hit Enter on a URL
title.ms: Apa Sebenarnya Berlaku Bila Anda Tekan Enter pada URL

summary.en: You type a web address, press Enter, and a page appears. It feels instant, but in that blink your browser makes a decision, asks a chain of servers for an address, sets up an encrypted connection, sends a request that may never reach the real website, and then turns raw text into pixels.
summary.ms: Anda menaip alamat web, menekan Enter, dan halaman muncul. Ia terasa serta-merta, tetapi dalam sekelip mata pelayar anda membuat keputusan, bertanya kepada beberapa pelayan tentang satu alamat, menyediakan sambungan yang disulitkan, menghantar permintaan yang mungkin tidak pernah sampai ke laman sebenar, dan kemudian menukar teks mentah menjadi piksel.

title.en: Scaling an App From 1 to 1 Million Users, Step by Step
title.ms: Kembangkan Aplikasi Daripada 1 kepada 1 Juta Pengguna, Langkah demi Langkah

summary.en: Lots of apps start the same way: one server, doing everything. So what actually changes on the way from your first user to your millionth? There's no magic number of users where you're supposed to add a cache or a second server.
summary.ms: Banyak aplikasi bermula dengan cara yang sama: satu server yang membuat semuanya. Jadi, apa yang sebenarnya berubah dari pengguna pertama anda hingga yang kesejuta? Tiada bilangan pengguna ajaib yang menentukan bila anda perlu menambah cache atau server kedua.

chapters.en: Stateless servers and a load balancer

cat > backup.sh <<'EOF'

if [ -f "$1" ]; then
  mkdir -p backup
  cp "$1" backup

else
  echo "no such file: $1"
  exit 1
fi
EOF

code.output:
bash: line 2: [-f: command not found

code.title: Version 6: check every copy
code.code:
touch plans.txt
cat > backup.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
save() {
  if cp "$1" backup; then
    echo "saved $1"
  else
    echo "NOT saved: $1"; status=1
  fi
}
status=0
mkdir -p backup || exit 1
for file in "$@"; do save "$file"; done
exit "$status"
EOF
chmod +x backup.sh
./backup.sh plans.txt plnas.txt || echo "not all"
code.output:
saved plans.txt
cp: cannot stat 'plnas.txt': No such file or directory
NOT saved: plnas.txt
not all

title.en: Linux for Beginners #4: 10 Command-Line Tips
title.ms: Linux untuk Pemula #4: 10 Tips Command Line

summary.en: Ten tips, counted down from ten to one, and the last is the one that protects your files. Each tip gets the same fair treatment: how it looks before, how it looks after, and the moment when you should leave it alone.
summary.ms: 10 tips, dikira mundur dari 10 hingga 1, dan yang terakhir ialah yang melindungi fail anda. Setiap tip mendapat layanan adil yang sama: rupanya sebelum, rupanya selepas, dan saat anda patut tidak menggunakannya.

code.title: Fix the default with None

    items.append(item)
    return items

code.title: Generator bodies start lazily
code.code:
events = []
def gen():
    events.append('body ran')
    yield 1
g = gen()
print('after call:', type(g).__name__, events)
print('first next:', next(g))
print('after next:', events)
code.output:
after call: generator []
first next: 1
after next: ['body ran']

code.title: yield pauses and preserves locals
code.code:
log = []
def gen():
    n = 10
    log.append('at first yield')
    yield n
    log.append('resumed')
    n += 5
    yield n
g = gen()
print(next(g), log)
print(next(g), log)

code.title: Slice an infinite generator
code.code:
from itertools import islice
def naturals():
    n = 1
    while True:
        yield n
        n += 1
print(list(islice(naturals(), 5)))

code.title: Delegate with yield from

    yield 1
    yield 2
def outer():
    yield 0
    yield from inner()
    yield 3
print(list(outer()))

code.title: __enter__ and __exit__ on a normal block
__exit__ runs when the block raises
__exit__ receives the exception
Returning True suppresses the exception
Write a manager with @contextmanager
code.code:
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def shopping():
    print("take list")
    yield ["milk", "bread"]
    print("put list away")

with shopping() as items:
    print(items)

code.title: Use try/finally around yield

code.title: Two managers exit in reverse order
code.code:
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def bag(name):
    print("open", name)
    yield
    print("close", name)

with bag("A"), bag("B"):
    print("pack groceries")
code.output:
open A
open B
pack groceries
close B
close A
